title: Comparison of Long-Term Effects Following Phacoemulsification Combined with Goniosynechialysis and Trabeculectomy in Patients with Primary Angle-Closure Glaucoma and Cataract

license.statement: CC BY-NC 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International License) - non-commercial, record kept private

indication: primary angle-closure glaucoma with coexisting cataract and synechial angle closure over more than 180 degrees; no prior eye surgery (retrospective, single centre, Chinese patients, one eye per patient)

groups.description: phacoemulsification with posterior chamber IOL combined with goniosynechialysis under intraoperative gonioscopy (viscoelastic and spatula)
fornix-based trabeculectomy with mitomycin C (no combined cataract surgery described); suture lysis and needling with 5-fluorouracil as postoperative care

notes: Study procedure is 'other' because the two arms are in different contexts; each group declares its own procedure (phaco-goniosynechialysis = angle_mims; trabeculectomy with MMC = trabeculectomy).
Both arms are established procedures compared retrospectively without an investigational agent or device declared experimental, so both are control groups.

Reference kind: patients were taking 2-4 antiglaucoma medications before surgery (Table 1 R7 and Table 3, median (Q1, Q3); Results text) and no washout is described, so the preoperative IOP is recorded as measured on the usual medication; the article does not state the medication status at the measurement explicitly.

In the phaco-GSL arm a subsequent trabeculectomy with MMC was indicated if IOP stayed above target on maximal medication; the article does not state whether such eyes were removed from later visit means (no outcome-defined exclusion is stated, so the per-visit means are kept).
Number of antiglaucoma medications (median (Q1, Q3)) is tabulated in Table 3 preoperatively and at final follow-up (not extracted).
Time conversions: 1 day = 0.0329 months, 1 week = 0.23 months.
